headline: Record revenue and profit on higher royalty volumes
summary_short: Revenue rose 3.9% q/q to $246.1 million and net income grew 7.7% to $153.9 million, or $2.23 per diluted share, as oil and gas royalty production hit a record 39.7 thousand Boe/d and the average realized price climbed to $42.17/Boe from $37.06/Boe.
summary_long: The company cited record consolidated net income, free cash flow, and oil-and-gas and produced-water royalty volumes. Revenue growth came from a $27.4 million rise in oil and gas royalty revenue plus higher easements and produced water royalties, partly offset by the prior quarter's $20.9 million land sale not recurring and a $7.1 million drop in water sales. Operating expenses were roughly flat q/q. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $215.6 million and free cash flow to $155.5 million. Total cash was roughly flat at $248.6 million. TPL is unhedged on commodity price, capturing the quarter's higher oil prices. No forward guidance was issued; the company declared its regular $0.60/share quarterly dividend.

drivers.explanation: CEO Tyler Glover said the company "delivered record results across major financial and operating metrics," citing record oil and gas royalty production and produced water royalty volumes plus an unhedged position that captured the quarter's higher oil prices.

Release attributes the q/q increase to a $27.4M rise in oil and gas royalty revenue, a $6.3M rise in easements/surface income, and a $3.5M rise in produced water royalties, partly offset by a $20.9M swing in land sales and a $7.1M drop in water sales.

Total operating expenses were roughly flat q/q ($54.2M vs $54.5M) — a $2.7M decrease in water service-related expenses was mostly offset by a $2.6M rise in depreciation, depletion and amortization — so operating income tracked the revenue increase almost dollar-for-dollar.
Grew in line with operating income; interest expense and other income were both little changed q/q.
Tracks the rise in pretax income; the effective tax rate was essentially flat q/q (20.5% vs 22.2%).

The reconciliation shows Q1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was reduced by a $20.9M land-sale-with-financing-arrangement deduction that did not recur in Q2, alongside the underlying EBITDA increase from higher royalty revenue.
Reflects higher net income and steady add-backs, partly offset by a rise in purchases of fixed assets to $21.9M from $7.3M q/q; company attributes free cash flow strength to record operating results.

Not explained in the release beyond the components of free cash flow; the $0.60/share dividend and land acquisitions in Shackelford, Jones, and Winkler Counties ($110.2 million aggregate) were funded largely from the quarter's cash generation, leaving the cash balance nearly unchanged.
Not explained in the release; consistent with retained-earnings growth from $153.9M of net income against the smaller $0.60/share dividend outflow.
Share count was essentially unchanged q/q; the release discloses no buyback or issuance activity this quarter.
